## TL;DR

Added a Pipeline view to the Work page: a horizontal race track with one lane
per task in `active` or `review` plus recently merged tasks, switched with a
Pipeline | Board toggle that mirrors the Inputs page switch and persists per
user. Board is the default and untouched. The stage mapping is a pure
view-model in `src/core/pipeline-view.ts` (33 tests), the four-line card and
track are two new components using theme tokens only, and a `board:pipeline`
shot fixture seeds every stage for review. Full `repoos check` passes,
including the hardcoded-colors guard and the rendered contrast audit.

## Work and rationale

The board buries live state — round counts, models, run host — in the task
panel, and its two columns say nothing about how far along a task is. The new
view answers "what is happening and how far along is it" at a glance: six
stage columns (Coding, Checks, Handoff, Review, Close-out, Merged), one lane
per task at 96px pitch, the card sitting in its current stage column. Position
is always a discrete stage, never a fake percentage.

Big decisions:

- **Pure core view-model.** `resolvePipelineCard(task-signals)` returns stage,
  state, step label, bounce count and dimming, with `isPipelineVisible`,
  `sortPipelineLanes` and `formatPipelineElapsed` beside it. The component only
  feeds it store signals. This made every stage, the sent-back case, stuck,
  held and the 10-minute merged window directly unit-testable.
- **States, not stages.** Stuck, needs-input, paused and held layer over the
  stage where the task stalled. Stuck reuses the board card's exact `tc-stuck`
  evidence (silent agent, stalled check/remote, telemetry mismatch) plus
  stalled close-out and failed Move to done; needs-input reuses
  `needsInputSurfaces`. No second rule, no drift.
- **Line 4 shares the panel's sources.** `taskRoundCounts` was extracted from
  `TaskDrawer.vue` into `lib/pipeline-card.ts` and the drawer now calls it —
  one counting rule for `extra.review_passes` / `review_rounds` /
  `dev_error_count`. Models go through `resolveEffectiveAgent`, host through
  the remote run/queue host with a `"this Mac"` fallback.
- **Lane order: priority, then longest in flight first.** Oldest `created_at`
  rides at the top so a stale lane is visible without scrolling; id breaks
  ties for frame stability.
- **Time in state reads `updated_at`** (`releasedAt` once merged) — the honest
  available signal, no new event stream.
- **Toggle copies InputsView** (same `.view-toggle` styles, no native `title`
  tooltips, `aria-pressed`), persisted under `repoos.work.view-mode`. Board is
  default; sort control, collapse button, filter bar and parked lists render
  board-only. The track reuses the board's reactive store, so SSE updates move
  cards with no extra wiring.
- **Fixture forces the view.** `board:pipeline` seeds nine lanes (every stage,
  stuck, held, sent-back with a red-verdict report, recently merged, one ready
  task for the queue count). WorkView renders Pipeline whenever a preview
  build carries `?shotState=board:pipeline`, regardless of mount order or the
  stored preference.

## Approaches tried

I first considered deriving stuck/held/needs-input inside the component, but
the board card already encodes those predicates across several store slices —
re-deriving would have created the exact second source of truth the task
forbids. Instead the component collects the same inputs (`activeEngineerCard-
Hint`, `needsInputSurfaces`, `isHoldActive`, pipeline role, check runs) and
hands them to the pure mapper. Similarly, handoff-vs-checks ambiguity is
resolved once in the mapper (any handoff signal wins; a lone `merge-gate` run
is Checks; agent-slot queueing stays in Coding) and written down in
`docs/pipeline-stage-mapping.md` with the other ambiguous cases.

For the Merged goal tint I used per-cell `var(--green-tint)` backgrounds on
contiguous 96px rows rather than an absolutely positioned backdrop — simpler,
and it reads as one full-height area. Hairlines are
`color-mix(in srgb, var(--txt) 7%, transparent)` borders, no lane backgrounds.

## Challenges and blockers

- The `repoos update --shots` call ran against the main checkout's board (the
  CLI reads main from inside a linked worktree), so the `## Shots` section
  landed on main's task copy, not the branch copy. Left as is: handoff syncs
  the canonical copy, and per AGENTS.md main's copy of `work/<id>-*.md` wins
  any merge.
- A scoped `repoos check` timed out once at 10 minutes behind a busy
  machine, then passed fully on retry (remote validation ran the tests).
  Worth knowing: the first failure in the same run was only `oxfmt --check`,
  fixed with `bun run fmt`.
- One test initially asserted the restored view synchronously after mount;
  Vue flushes the `v-if` swap on the next tick, so it awaits `$nextTick` now.

## Key learnings

- The `hardcoded-colors` guard only flags hex literals and `rgba(255,…)` in
  `<style>` blocks — `color-mix()` with theme tokens and token-only chip
  styles pass cleanly, and the rendered contrast audit passed in all 16 theme
  scopes with the new amber/red/green chips, since they reuse the board's
  existing token pairs.
- `shotFixtureContainer` maps the `board:` prefix to `task-card`
  automatically, so the new fixture needed no capture-plumbing changes beyond
  its seed case and ID registration.
- A `state` fixture cannot rely on `localStorage` set during fixture
  application (App applies fixtures after views mount), so the view reads the
  reactive `route.query.shotState` on preview builds instead — deterministic
  for both cold loads and capture navigations.
